pr.title: Answer a question by its option's number, even when you edit the option's words
pr.head: 09bc6d9e506902272164e878d85e203e500e2c89

summary: Projector's panel shows an agent's open questions. When you press one of a question's options, the panel puts the quoted question and the option in your prompt, and sending that prompt records the answer. Before this change, the panel recognized the answer only when the option's words were unchanged on their line. Editing them, even slightly, turned the answer into a reply, so the question stayed open.

This change puts the option's number in front of its words, as the drawer already shows it, for example 2: Add a budget. The number is now what answers, so you can reword the option and still answer with it. Text without a number answers by the old rule, so an option typed by hand still works.

Text under the quoteResult
2: Add a budget of threeAnswers option 2
2:Answers option 2
Add a budget on its own lineAnswers by words, as before
3: … on a two-option questionReply
1:30 tomorrowReply (a time, not a number)
A line of your own, then 2: …Reply
Requests keep reading their outcome by words, because a request's option digits shift when its start action comes and goes.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Quote: the [3] "subject" line the panel writes for an item.
  • Drawer: the panel's expanded view of one item, with its option buttons.
  • Proposal: the panel's record of what a drawer put in the prompt, used to tell apart two questions with the same subject.
  • Stale: a proposal made before its question was revised. It can only reply.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The Projector review of 09bc6d9 found no defects. The gate passed: plugin validation, 263 hook tests, and the check CI job.

groups.title: Reading the answer from a prompt
groups.kicker: How the panel finds the option a sent prompt picks
intro: readPrompt in hooks/inbox.ts reads each sent prompt and decides, for each quoted question, whether the text below the quote answers it, replies to it, or says you don't understand it. This group changes the answer rule from matching an option's words to matching its number first.

Two helpers carry it. optionIn now returns the option's index: a leading number picks that option, and without one it falls back to the old word match. picks decides whether the text matches what a particular drawer put there, which is how the panel tells apart two questions that share a subject.

files.note: The new number rule in optionIn and picks, and the ask tool's description of what an agent receives.

checks.text: The lookahead after the colon is what stops a time such as 1:30 from reading as option 1. Numbers start at 1, so 0: never matches.
A number above the question's option count returns undefined rather than falling back to the words, so it replies. Checked by reading and by the test suite, which passed at this head.
Discuss proposals, whose answer is empty, still match through the separate one.answer === '' branch of the source lookup, so the number check does not break them. Checked by reading the call site.
When a question was revised, the panel can hold both a stale and a fresh proposal with the same number. findLast takes the fresh one because propose appends it last.

files.note: New cases for numbered answers, edited words, two questions sharing a subject, and the numbers that still reply.

groups.title: Filling the prompt from the drawer
groups.kicker: The drawer writes the number before the option's words
intro: When you press an option, the panel's pick handler now writes pickOf(index, choice), the number and the words, into the prompt and records the same text as the drawer's proposal. The number comes from the same question.choices index that optionIn reads back, so the digit you see and the letter recorded agree.

files.note: pick takes the option's index and fills pickOf's text.
Existing panel tests now expect the numbered fill, and one now edits the words before sending.
